cases.counterfactual_program:
(rule!
  (lambda (g)
    (let* ((pivot (first (find-color g 2)))
           (pr (first pivot))
           (pc (second pivot))
           (markers (find-color g 1)))
      (define (rotations p)
        (let* ((dr (- (first p) pr)) (dc (- (second p) pc)))
          (list (list dr dc) (list dc (- dr))
                (list (- dr) (- dc)) (list (- dc) dr))))
      (define (visible-count p)
        (length (filter (lambda (d)
          (in-bounds? (+ pr (first d)) (+ pc (second d)) (rows g) (cols g)))
          (rotations p))))
      (define selected (foldl (lambda (p best) (if (> (visible-count p) (visible-count best)) p best)) (first markers) (rest markers)))
      (foldl (lambda (d acc)
        (let ((nr (+ pr (first d))) (nc (+ pc (second d))))
          (if (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g)) (set-cell acc nr nc 1) acc)))
        g (rotations selected)))))

intermediate: The input-dependent unique blue source marker whose visible rotated orbit has the minimum cell count, together with that exact orbit and count.
step_a: For every blue source marker, compute its four 0/90/180/270-degree rotations about the unique red pivot, filter them to the input bounds, and retain the resulting visible orbit and visible-cell count.
step_b: Paint only the in-bounds cells of the selected intermediate orbit blue while preserving all original cells and the red pivot.
why_b_depends_on_a: The orbit painted by B cannot be chosen until A has compared clipping counts for every source marker. Replacing the minimum-count intermediate with the maximum-count (least-clipped) marker selects a different complete orbit and changes the protected-Racket final grid.
